title: Clashing talks as clique rows

blocks.text: A utility's training week (not GridCap) has more proposed talks than it can run. Each talk has a speaker, a value, and a number of hours of the one shared demonstration lab, which is open for $`H`$ hours over the week. Two rules: a speaker gives at most one talk, and the lab hours of **any two** accepted talks must fit together within $`H`$ (the lab is booked in pairs of sessions; that is the planners' rule, take it as given). With $`x_t \in \{0, 1\}`$ for "talk $`t`$ is accepted", the model maximizes $`\sum_t v_t\, x_t`$.

items: `clashes(talks, lab_hours)`: the pairs of talks that no allowed programme accepts together, as a set of `frozenset({name, name})`;
`add_clash_rows(model, x, pairs)`: rows that refuse exactly those pairs, written so the LP bound is as tight as you can make it, and returning how many rows were added.

blocks.text: Pair rows $`x_a + x_b \le 1`$ would refuse the right programmes, but the lesson showed why they leave the LP loose. Decide on paper which groups of talks can share one "at most one" row, why that row is valid, and how to cover every clash with such rows. Then write the rows with labels before coding.
The tests try every programme of five talks against the rules, so any correct set of rows passes them; two of them also check the LP bound. About twenty lines.

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Talk:
    name: str
    speaker: str
    lab_hours: int             # hours of the shared lab the talk's demonstration needs
    value: int


def clashes(talks: list[Talk], lab_hours: int) -> set[frozenset[str]]:
    """Pairs of talks no programme can accept together."""
    # TODO: the pairs that clash, and why.
    return set()


def add_clash_rows(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, pairs: set[frozenset[str]]) -> int:
    """Cover every clash with a row 'at most one of these talks', as few and as wide as greedily found."""
    # TODO: rows that cover every clash.
    return 0


def build(talks: list[Talk], lab_hours: int, *, integer: bool = True) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="programme")
    x = {t.name: model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=1, is_integer=integer, name=f"x_{t.name}") for t in talks}
    add_clash_rows(model, x, clashes(talks, lab_hours))
    model.maximize(sum(t.value * x[t.name] for t in talks))
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    talks = [Talk("T1", "ana", 5, 3), Talk("T2", "ben", 4, 2), Talk("T3", "ana", 1, 1)]
    print(sorted(sorted(p) for p in clashes(talks, 8)))

cases.says: every programme the two rules allow is allowed, and every other refused
two talks by one speaker clash even when the lab has room for both
two talks whose lab hours add up to exactly the lab's hours may both run
talks that clash two by two, for whatever reason, share one row, so the LP cannot accept half of each

origin.section: A Clique of Conflicts Is One Valid Row, Stronger Than Its Pairs

concepts: a set of pairwise conflicts gives one row that implies its pair rows and cuts more
pairs no allowed plan uses together come from once, alternative and capacity rows
